```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(fixest)
library(ggcorrplot)
library(purrr)
library(lmtest)
library(zoo)
library(e1071)
```

---

# Part 1 — Data Loading and Preprocessing

The data contains slang-level adoption rates. Within each time window and subreddit
there are multiple slang terms. The forecast horizon is defined in calendar periods,
not row positions, and targets are joined by key. We keep only slang-subreddit pairs
whose eligible predictor sequence is **continuous** (no gaps).

## 1.1 Load and validate

```{r load}
df_raw <- read.csv("./slang-level-df.csv")

KEY_VARS <- c("subreddit", "slang", "time_idx")
COUNT_VARS <- c(
  "active_user_count", "active_adopter_count",
  "new_users_count", "new_adopter_count"
)
COVARIATES_RAW <- c(
  "mean_betweenness", "mean_degree",
  "semantic_dispersion", "effective_topics"
)

# The models below are compared on one explicit common sample. If a model-specific
# sample is desired, define its required covariates separately instead of using a
# blanket drop_na() across the whole data frame.
REQUIRED_CURRENT_VARS <- c(KEY_VARS, "time", COUNT_VARS, COVARIATES_RAW)

duplicate_keys <- df_raw %>%
  count(across(all_of(KEY_VARS)), name = "n") %>%
  filter(n > 1)
stopifnot(nrow(duplicate_keys) == 0)

# Each month must map one-to-one to time_idx, and the index must advance monthly.
time_map <- df_raw %>%
  distinct(time, time_idx) %>%
  arrange(time_idx) %>%
  mutate(
    parsed_month = as.Date(paste0(time, "-01")),
    month_number = as.integer(format(parsed_month, "%Y")) * 12L +
      as.integer(format(parsed_month, "%m"))
  )
stopifnot(
  nrow(time_map) == n_distinct(time_map$time),
  nrow(time_map) == n_distinct(time_map$time_idx),
  !anyNA(time_map$parsed_month),
  all(diff(time_map$time_idx) == diff(time_map$month_number))
)

# Counts used as outcomes or exposure components must be finite, non-negative integers.
for (v in COUNT_VARS) {
  stopifnot(
    is.numeric(df_raw[[v]]),
    all(is.finite(df_raw[[v]])),
    all(df_raw[[v]] >= 0),
    all(df_raw[[v]] == floor(df_raw[[v]]))
  )
}

df_raw %>% head()
```


## 1.2 Create calendar-aligned targets and exposure

The stated outcome is one calendar period ahead, so the default horizon is 1.
Change `FORECAST_HORIZON` to 22 if a 22-month outcome is intended; the keyed join
will remain correctly aligned even when a pair has missing observations.

```{r targets_and_exposure}
FORECAST_HORIZON <- 1L
stopifnot(length(FORECAST_HORIZON) == 1, FORECAST_HORIZON >= 1)

target_lookup <- df_raw %>%
  transmute(
    subreddit,
    slang,
    target_time_idx = time_idx,
    target_time = time,
    target_new_adopters_count = new_adopter_count,
    target_active_adopters_count = active_adopter_count
  )

df_prepared <- df_raw %>%
  mutate(
    target_time_idx = time_idx + FORECAST_HORIZON,
    eligible_user_exposure =
      active_user_count - active_adopter_count +
      new_users_count - new_adopter_count
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    target_lookup,
    by = c("subreddit", "slang", "target_time_idx")
  )

invalid_exposure_n <- df_prepared %>%
  summarise(n = sum(!is.finite(eligible_user_exposure) |
                      eligible_user_exposure <= 0, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  pull(n)
cat("Rows with invalid exposure before filtering:", invalid_exposure_n, "\n")
```


## 1.3 Define the eligible common sample

```{r}
df_eligible <- df_prepared %>%
  drop_na(all_of(REQUIRED_CURRENT_VARS)) %>%
  filter(
    is.finite(eligible_user_exposure),
    eligible_user_exposure > 0
  )

cat("Input rows:", nrow(df_raw), "\n")
cat("Rows in common complete-case/exposure sample:", nrow(df_eligible), "\n")
```


## 1.4 Keep only no-gap pairs

Continuity is evaluated before rows without a future target are removed. This prevents
the target-horizon truncation from hiding gaps at the end of a pair's history.

```{r continuity}
slang_continuity <- df_eligible %>%
  group_by(slang, subreddit) %>%
  summarise(
    n_periods = n_distinct(time_idx),
    span      = max(time_idx) - min(time_idx) + 1,
    has_gap   = n_periods != span,
    .groups   = "drop"
  )

cat("Gap summary (TRUE = has a gap):\n")
print(table(slang_continuity$has_gap))

continuous_pairs <- slang_continuity %>%
  filter(!has_gap) %>%
  select(slang, subreddit)

df_nogaps <- df_eligible %>%
  semi_join(continuous_pairs, by = c("slang", "subreddit")) %>%
  drop_na(
    target_time, target_new_adopters_count,
    target_active_adopters_count
  )

stopifnot(all(
  df_nogaps$target_time_idx - df_nogaps$time_idx == FORECAST_HORIZON
))

cat("\nSlangs before:", n_distinct(df_eligible$slang),
    "  after:", n_distinct(df_nogaps$slang), "\n")
cat("Rows  before:", nrow(df_eligible),
    "  after:", nrow(df_nogaps), "\n")
```

## 1.5 Remove singleton groups for the fixed effects actually modeled

The models use `subreddit ^ time_idx` and `slang` fixed effects. Singleton removal
is therefore based on those groups and is repeated until no new singleton is created.

```{r fixed_effect_sample}
remove_fe_singletons <- function(data) {
  repeat {
    n_before <- nrow(data)

    data <- data %>%
      add_count(subreddit, time_idx, name = ".n_subreddit_time") %>%
      add_count(slang, name = ".n_slang") %>%
      filter(.n_subreddit_time > 1, .n_slang > 1) %>%
      select(-.n_subreddit_time, -.n_slang)

    if (nrow(data) == n_before) return(data)
  }
}

n_before_fe_filter <- nrow(df_nogaps)
df_nogaps <- remove_fe_singletons(df_nogaps)

cat("Rows removed as fixed-effect singletons:",
    n_before_fe_filter - nrow(df_nogaps), "\n")
cat("Final prepared rows:", nrow(df_nogaps), "\n")
cat("Final subreddits:", n_distinct(df_nogaps$subreddit), "\n")
```

## 2.1  Distribution of raw covariates

```{r raw_distributions}
par(mfrow = c(3, 3))
for (v in COVARIATES_RAW) {

}

cat("\nSkewness and mean/median ratio:\n")
sapply(COVARIATES_RAW, function(v) {
  c(
    skew            = skewness(df_nogaps[[v]], na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_med_ratio  = mean(df_nogaps[[v]], na.rm = TRUE) /
                      median(df_nogaps[[v]], na.rm = TRUE)
  )
})
```

## 2.2 Transform and scale the final analysis sample

The raw variables remain available in `df_nogaps`. Network covariates are log-transformed
and all four covariates are standardized only after the final analysis sample is fixed.

```{r transform_and_scale}
df_model <- df_nogaps %>%
  mutate(
    mean_degree = log1p(mean_degree),
    mean_betweenness = log1p(mean_betweenness)
  ) %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(COVARIATES_RAW), ~ as.numeric(scale(.x))))
```

```{r corr_plot}

feature_mat <- cor(df_model[, CORR_VARS], use = "complete.obs")

ggcorrplot(
```

# Part 3 — Model Fitting

All models use the same no-gap, transformed and scaled dataset (`df_model`).

- **m0**: model with intercept only
- **m1**: model with network features only
- **m2**: model with network features and semantic dispersion
- **m3**: model with network features and topic intensity
- **m4**: model with network features and both linguistic features
- **m5**: model with linguistic features only


```{r model_m1}
m1 <- fenegbin(
  target_new_adopters_count ~
    mean_betweenness  + mean_degree | subreddit ^ time_idx + slang,
  offset  = ~log(eligible_user_exposure),
  data    = df_model,
  cluster = ~subreddit
)

summary(m1)
```

```{r model_m0}

df_used <- df_model[obs(m1), ]
df_removed <- df_model[-obs(m1), ]

m0 <- fenegbin(
  target_new_adopters_count ~ 1,
  data    = df_used,
  cluster = ~subreddit,
  offset  = ~log(eligible_user_exposure)
)

summary(m0)
```

```{r model_m2}
)

summary(m2)
```

```{r lr_test}
lrtest(m0, m1, m2, m3, m4)
```

## 3.1 Monte Carlo robustness to LLM classification error

This analysis treats the observed future `new_adopter_count` as an imperfect binary
classification aggregated to a count. In the analysis-ready data, that future count is
stored as `target_new_adopters_count`; the current-period `new_adopter_count` and every
covariate remain unchanged. The simulation uses the same rows, offset, fixed effects,
and clustered negative-binomial specification as `m4`.

Let $q$ be the observed prevalence. The estimated true prevalence $p$ is first
calculated using the Rogan--Gladen correction:

\[
p = \frac{q + Sp - 1}{Se + Sp - 1}.
\]

Given sensitivity $Se$, specificity $Sp$, and corrected prevalence $p$, the
probability that an observed adopter is truly an adopter is

\[
PPV = \frac{Se\,p}{Se\,p + (1-Sp)(1-p)}.
\]

Among observed non-adopters, the corresponding probability of being a false negative is

\[
P(T=1 \mid O=0) =
\frac{(1-Se)p}{(1-Se)p + Sp(1-p)}.
\]

### Validate classification parameters

```{r mc_validate_parameters}
validate_classification_parameters <- function(
    sensitivity, specificity, prevalence) {
  parameters <- c(
    sensitivity = sensitivity,
    specificity = specificity,
    prevalence = prevalence
  )

  if (anyNA(parameters)) {
    stop(
      paste0(
        "Monte Carlo analysis cannot run: set SENSITIVITY, SPECIFICITY, ",
        "and OBSERVED_PREVALENCE to numeric values in [0, 1]."
      ),
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }

  if (!is.numeric(parameters) || any(!is.finite(parameters)) ||
      any(parameters < 0 | parameters > 1)) {
    stop(
      "SENSITIVITY, SPECIFICITY, and OBSERVED_PREVALENCE must all be finite numeric values in [0, 1].",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }

  invisible(parameters)
}

# Monte Carlo classification-error inputs. Replace NA with validated values
SENSITIVITY <- 0.9344
SPECIFICITY <- 0.9294
OBSERVED_PREVALENCE <- 0.1841

N_MONTE_CARLO_SIMULATIONS <- 100L
MONTE_CARLO_SEED <- 20260830L

validate_classification_parameters(
  SENSITIVITY, SPECIFICITY, OBSERVED_PREVALENCE
)
```

### Modular simulation and model functions

```{r mc_functions}
calculate_corrected_prevalence <- function(
    sensitivity, specificity, observed_prevalence) {
  denominator <- sensitivity + specificity - 1

  if (denominator <= 0) {
    stop(
      "Prevalence correction requires SENSITIVITY + SPECIFICITY > 1.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }

  corrected_prevalence <-
    (observed_prevalence + specificity - 1) / denominator

  if (corrected_prevalence < 0 || corrected_prevalence > 1) {
    stop(
      paste0(
        "The supplied sensitivity, specificity, and observed prevalence are ",
        "incompatible: the corrected prevalence is ",
        round(corrected_prevalence, 4), "."
      ),
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }

  corrected_prevalence
}

calculate_prevalence_adjusted_ppv <- function(
    sensitivity, specificity, prevalence) {
  numerator <- sensitivity * prevalence
  denominator <- numerator + (1 - specificity) * (1 - prevalence)

  if (denominator <= 0) {
    stop(
      "PPV is undefined for the supplied sensitivity, specificity, and prevalence.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }

  numerator / denominator
}

simulate_corrected_adopter_counts <- function(
    observed_new_adopter_count,
    eligible_population,
    sensitivity,
    specificity,
    prevalence,
    ppv) {
  if (length(observed_new_adopter_count) != length(eligible_population)) {
    stop("Observed counts and eligible populations must have equal length.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  if (anyNA(observed_new_adopter_count) || anyNA(eligible_population) ||
      any(observed_new_adopter_count < 0) || any(eligible_population < 0)) {
    stop("Observed counts and eligible populations must be non-negative and non-missing.", call. = FALSE)
  }

  observed_count <- as.integer(round(observed_new_adopter_count))
  eligible_count <- as.integer(floor(eligible_population))

  # A classified-positive count cannot exceed the population being classified.
  # This cap affects only the simulated copy, never the original analysis data.
  observed_count_for_simulation <- pmin(observed_count, eligible_count)
  observed_negative_count <- eligible_count - observed_count_for_simulation

  true_positive_count <- rbinom(
    n = length(observed_count_for_simulation),
    size = observed_count_for_simulation,
    prob = ppv
  )

  false_negative_numerator <- (1 - sensitivity) * prevalence
  false_negative_denominator <-
    false_negative_numerator + specificity * (1 - prevalence)
  false_negative_probability <- if (false_negative_denominator == 0) {
    0
  } else {
    false_negative_numerator / false_negative_denominator
  }

  false_negative_count <- rbinom(
    n = length(observed_negative_count),
    size = observed_negative_count,
    prob = false_negative_probability
  )

  corrected_count <- true_positive_count + false_negative_count
  corrected_count <- pmax(0L, pmin(corrected_count, eligible_count))

  stopifnot(
    all(corrected_count >= 0),
    all(corrected_count <= eligible_count)
  )

  corrected_count
}

fit_adoption_regression <- function(data) {
  fenegbin(
    target_new_adopters_count ~
      mean_betweenness + mean_degree + effective_topics + semantic_dispersion |
      subreddit ^ time_idx + slang,
    data = data,
    offset = ~log(eligible_user_exposure),
    cluster = ~subreddit
  )
}

summarize_monte_carlo_results <- function(
    simulation_results, original_model, covariates) {
  original_table <- coeftable(original_model)
  missing_original_terms <- setdiff(covariates, rownames(original_table))
  if (length(missing_original_terms) > 0) {
    stop(
      paste("Original model is missing:", paste(missing_original_terms, collapse = ", ")),
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }

  original_coefficients <- tibble(
    term = covariates,
    original_coefficient = original_table[covariates, 1]
  )

  simulation_results %>%
    left_join(original_coefficients, by = "term") %>%
    group_by(term, original_coefficient) %>%
    summarise(
      median_simulated_coefficient = median(estimate),
      simulated_q025 = quantile(estimate, 0.025),
      simulated_q975 = quantile(estimate, 0.975),
      proportion_same_sign = mean(sign(estimate) == sign(original_coefficient)),
      proportion_p_below_005 = mean(p_value < 0.05),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}
```

### Run 100 simulations

```{r mc_run}
MC_COVARIATES <- c(
  "mean_betweenness", "mean_degree", "mean_local_clustering",
  "semantic_dispersion", "effective_topics"
)
MODEL_COVARIATES <- c(
  "mean_betweenness", "mean_degree",
  "semantic_dispersion", "effective_topics"
)

stopifnot(all(MC_COVARIATES %in% names(df_used)))

ESTIMATED_TRUE_PREVALENCE <- calculate_corrected_prevalence(
  SENSITIVITY, SPECIFICITY, OBSERVED_PREVALENCE
)

MC_PPV <- calculate_prevalence_adjusted_ppv(
  SENSITIVITY, SPECIFICITY, ESTIMATED_TRUE_PREVALENCE
)

false_negative_numerator <-
  (1 - SENSITIVITY) * ESTIMATED_TRUE_PREVALENCE
false_negative_denominator <-
  false_negative_numerator +
  SPECIFICITY * (1 - ESTIMATED_TRUE_PREVALENCE)
MC_FALSE_NEGATIVE_PROBABILITY <- if (false_negative_denominator == 0) {
  0
} else {
  false_negative_numerator / false_negative_denominator
}

cat(
  "Estimated true prevalence after misclassification correction:",
  round(ESTIMATED_TRUE_PREVALENCE, 4), "\n"
)
cat("Monte Carlo PPV:", round(MC_PPV, 4), "\n")
cat(
  "False-negative probability among observed negatives:",
  round(MC_FALSE_NEGATIVE_PROBABILITY, 4), "\n"
)
cat(
  "Rows whose observed future count exceeds the eligible population and will be capped in simulated copies:",
  sum(df_used$target_new_adopters_count > df_used$eligible_user_exposure), "\n"
)

set.seed(MONTE_CARLO_SEED)

monte_carlo_results <- map_dfr(
  seq_len(N_MONTE_CARLO_SIMULATIONS),
  function(simulation_id) {
    simulated_data <- df_used
    simulated_data$target_new_adopters_count <-
      simulate_corrected_adopter_counts(
        observed_new_adopter_count = df_used$target_new_adopters_count,
        eligible_population = df_used$eligible_user_exposure,
        sensitivity = SENSITIVITY,
        specificity = SPECIFICITY,
        prevalence = ESTIMATED_TRUE_PREVALENCE,
        ppv = MC_PPV
      )

    # Explicitly verify that current-period counts and all covariates are untouched.
    stopifnot(
      identical(simulated_data$new_adopter_count, df_used$new_adopter_count),
      all(vapply(
        MC_COVARIATES,
        function(v) identical(simulated_data[[v]], df_used[[v]]),
        logical(1)
      ))
    )

    simulated_model <- tryCatch(
      fit_adoption_regression(simulated_data),
      error = function(e) {
        stop(
          sprintf("Monte Carlo simulation %d failed: %s", simulation_id, e$message),
          call. = FALSE
        )
      }
    )

    simulation_table <- coeftable(simulated_model)
    missing_terms <- setdiff(MODEL_COVARIATES, rownames(simulation_table))
    if (length(missing_terms) > 0) {
      stop(
        sprintf(
          "Simulation %d is missing coefficient(s): %s",
          simulation_id, paste(missing_terms, collapse = ", ")
        ),
        call. = FALSE
      )
    }

    if (simulation_id %% 25L == 0L) {
      cat("Completed", simulation_id, "of", N_MONTE_CARLO_SIMULATIONS, "simulations\n")
    }

    tibble(
      simulation = simulation_id,
      term = MODEL_COVARIATES,
      estimate = simulation_table[MODEL_COVARIATES, 1],
      std_error = simulation_table[MODEL_COVARIATES, 2],
      p_value = simulation_table[MODEL_COVARIATES, 4]
    )
  }
)

stopifnot(
  n_distinct(monte_carlo_results$simulation) == N_MONTE_CARLO_SIMULATIONS,
  nrow(monte_carlo_results) ==
    N_MONTE_CARLO_SIMULATIONS * length(MODEL_COVARIATES)
)
```

### Monte Carlo robustness summary

```{r mc_summary}
monte_carlo_summary <- summarize_monte_carlo_results(
  monte_carlo_results,
  original_model = m4,
  covariates = MODEL_COVARIATES
)

knitr::kable(
  monte_carlo_summary,
  digits = 3,
  col.names = c(
    "Covariate", "Original beta", "Median simulated beta",
    "2.5% quantile", "97.5% quantile", "Same-sign proportion",
    "Proportion p < 0.05"
  ),
  caption = "Monte Carlo robustness to LLM classification error"
)
```

# Part 4 — Coefficient Paths Across Forecast Horizons

This section estimates the full model (`m4`) separately for outcomes 1 through 30
calendar months ahead. To make coefficients comparable across horizons, every model
uses the same balanced set of current-period observations and the same covariate
standardization. The outcome changes with the horizon; the predictors and exposure do not.

## 4.1 Construct a balanced multi-horizon sample

```{r horizon_sample}
MAX_HORIZON <- 30L
HORIZONS <- seq_len(MAX_HORIZON)

CURRENT_MODEL_VARS <- c(REQUIRED_CURRENT_VARS, "eligible_user_exposure")

balanced_candidates <- df_eligible %>%
  semi_join(continuous_pairs, by = c("slang", "subreddit")) %>%
  select(all_of(CURRENT_MODEL_VARS))

# Identify current observations that have an exactly keyed outcome at every horizon.
horizon_availability <- balanced_candidates %>%
  select(all_of(KEY_VARS)) %>%
  crossing(horizon = HORIZONS) %>%
  mutate(target_time_idx = time_idx + horizon) %>%
  inner_join(
    target_lookup %>% select(subreddit, slang, target_time_idx),
    by = c("subreddit", "slang", "target_time_idx")
  )

balanced_keys <- horizon_availability %>%
  count(across(all_of(KEY_VARS)), name = "n_horizons") %>%
  filter(n_horizons == length(HORIZONS)) %>%
  select(all_of(KEY_VARS))

balanced_current <- balanced_candidates %>%
  semi_join(balanced_keys, by = KEY_VARS) %>%
  remove_fe_singletons()

# Transform and standardize once so a one-unit change has the same meaning at every horizon.
balanced_current_model <- balanced_current %>%
  mutate(
    mean_degree = log1p(mean_degree),
    mean_betweenness = log1p(mean_betweenness)
  ) %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(COVARIATES_RAW), ~ as.numeric(scale(.x))))

horizon_model_data <- balanced_current_model %>%
  crossing(horizon = HORIZONS) %>%
  mutate(target_time_idx = time_idx + horizon) %>%
  inner_join(
    target_lookup,
    by = c("subreddit", "slang", "target_time_idx")
  )

stopifnot(
  nrow(horizon_model_data) == nrow(balanced_current_model) * length(HORIZONS),
  all(horizon_model_data$target_time_idx - horizon_model_data$time_idx ==
        horizon_model_data$horizon)
)

cat("Balanced current-period observations per horizon:",
    nrow(balanced_current_model), "\n")
```

## 4.2 Fit the full model at each horizon

```{r horizon_models}
fit_horizon_model <- function(h) {
  data_h <- horizon_model_data %>% filter(horizon == h)

  fit <- fenegbin(
    target_new_adopters_count ~
      mean_betweenness + mean_degree + effective_topics + semantic_dispersion |
      subreddit ^ time_idx + slang,
    data = data_h,
    offset = ~log(eligible_user_exposure),
    cluster = ~subreddit
  )

  coefficient_table <- coeftable(fit)

  beta_table <- tibble(
    horizon = h,
    term = rownames(coefficient_table),
    estimate = coefficient_table[, 1],
    std_error = coefficient_table[, 2],
    conf_low = estimate - qnorm(0.975) * std_error,
    conf_high = estimate + qnorm(0.975) * std_error,
    observations = nobs(fit)
  ) %>%
    filter(term %in% COVARIATES_RAW)

  list(model = fit, betas = beta_table)
}

horizon_results <- set_names(HORIZONS) %>%
  map(fit_horizon_model)

# Named model list for inspecting any individual horizon, e.g. summary(horizon_fits[["15"]]).
horizon_fits <- horizon_results %>% map("model")
horizon_betas <- horizon_results %>% map_dfr("betas")

horizon_betas
```

## 4.4 Early-versus-late persistence

The descriptive persistence measure compares the average coefficient over horizons
1--5 with the average over horizons 26--30:

\[
\bar{\beta}_{\text{early}} = \frac{1}{5}\sum_{h=1}^{5}\beta_h,
\qquad
\bar{\beta}_{\text{late}} = \frac{1}{5}\sum_{h=26}^{30}\beta_h,
\qquad
\Delta = \bar{\beta}_{\text{late}} - \bar{\beta}_{\text{early}}.
\]

A positive $\Delta$ means the coefficient becomes more positive at long horizons;
a negative $\Delta$ means it becomes more negative. This calculation requires
`MAX_HORIZON >= 30`.

```{r persistence_summary}
EARLY_HORIZONS <- 1:5
LATE_HORIZONS <- 26:30

stopifnot(all(c(EARLY_HORIZONS, LATE_HORIZONS) %in% HORIZONS))

persistence_summary <- horizon_betas %>%
  filter(horizon %in% c(EARLY_HORIZONS, LATE_HORIZONS)) %>%
  mutate(
    window = case_when(
      horizon %in% EARLY_HORIZONS ~ "early",
      horizon %in% LATE_HORIZONS ~ "late"
    )
  ) %>%
  group_by(term, window) %>%
  summarise(mean_beta = mean(estimate), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = window, values_from = mean_beta) %>%
  transmute(
    predictor = unname(TERM_LABELS[term]),
    beta_early = early,
    beta_late = late,
    delta = beta_late - beta_early
  ) %>%
  arrange(match(predictor, unname(TERM_LABELS[FACET_ORDER])))

knitr::kable(
  persistence_summary,
  digits = 3,
  col.names = c(
    "Predictor", "Mean beta, h = 1--5",
    "Mean beta, h = 26--30", "Delta (late - early)"
  ),
  caption = "Descriptive early-versus-late coefficient persistence"
)
```

```{r persistence_interpretation, results='asis'}
semantic_result <- persistence_summary %>%
  filter(predictor == "Semantic Dispersion")
degree_result <- persistence_summary %>%
  filter(predictor == "Degree Centrality")
betweenness_result <- persistence_summary %>%
  filter(predictor == "Betweenness Centrality")

cat(sprintf(
  paste0(
    "> Semantic dispersion changes from approximately %.2f at short horizons ",
    "to %.2f at long horizons, while degree centrality changes from %.2f to %.2f ",
    "and betweenness centrality remains positive (%.2f early and %.2f late).\n"
  ),
  semantic_result$beta_early,
  semantic_result$beta_late,
  degree_result$beta_early,
  degree_result$beta_late,
  betweenness_result$beta_early,
  betweenness_result$beta_late
))
```

### Joint Wald test

The horizon-specific models reuse the same observations, so their coefficient estimates
are correlated. Adding their separate standard errors would therefore give an invalid
test. The model below stacks all horizons, interacts every predictor and fixed effect
with horizon, and clusters by subreddit. Its covariance matrix supports the Wald test
$H_0: \bar{\beta}_{\text{late}} = \bar{\beta}_{\text{early}}$.

```{r joint_horizon_model}
joint_horizon_data <- horizon_model_data %>%
  mutate(
    horizon_subreddit_time = interaction(
      horizon, subreddit, time_idx, drop = TRUE
    ),
    horizon_slang = interaction(horizon, slang, drop = TRUE)
  )

joint_horizon_model <- fenegbin(
  target_new_adopters_count ~
    i(horizon, mean_betweenness) +
    i(horizon, mean_degree) +
    i(horizon, effective_topics) +
    i(horizon, semantic_dispersion) |
    horizon_subreddit_time + horizon_slang,
  data = joint_horizon_data,
  offset = ~log(eligible_user_exposure),
  cluster = ~subreddit
)
```

```{r persistence_wald_test}
early_late_wald <- function(model, term, early_horizons, late_horizons) {
  estimates <- coef(model)
  covariance <- vcov(model)[names(estimates), names(estimates), drop = FALSE]

  early_names <- paste0("horizon::", early_horizons, ":", term)
  late_names <- paste0("horizon::", late_horizons, ":", term)
  required_names <- c(early_names, late_names)
  stopifnot(all(required_names %in% names(estimates)))

  contrast <- setNames(rep(0, length(estimates)), names(estimates))
  contrast[early_names] <- -1 / length(early_names)
  contrast[late_names] <- 1 / length(late_names)

  delta <- sum(contrast * estimates)
  delta_se <- sqrt(drop(t(contrast) %*% covariance %*% contrast))
  wald_chisq <- (delta / delta_se)^2

  tibble(
    term = term,
    joint_beta_early = mean(estimates[early_names]),
    joint_beta_late = mean(estimates[late_names]),
    delta = delta,
    std_error = delta_se,
    wald_chisq = wald_chisq,
    p_value = pchisq(wald_chisq, df = 1, lower.tail = FALSE)
  )
}

persistence_wald <- map_dfr(
  COVARIATES_RAW,
  ~ early_late_wald(
    joint_horizon_model, .x, EARLY_HORIZONS, LATE_HORIZONS
  )
) %>%
  transmute(
    predictor = unname(TERM_LABELS[term]),
    joint_beta_early,
    joint_beta_late,
    delta,
    std_error,
    wald_chisq,
    p_value
  ) %>%
  arrange(match(predictor, unname(TERM_LABELS[FACET_ORDER])))

knitr::kable(
  persistence_wald,
  digits = 3,
  col.names = c(
    "Predictor", "Joint early beta", "Joint late beta", "Delta",
    "SE(Delta)", "Wald chi-squared", "p-value"
  ),
  caption = "Joint Wald tests of equal early and late average coefficients"
)
```
